title: Robustness of Real-Space Topology in Moiré Systems
summary: Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.

title: Ab Initio Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo in the Thermodynamic Limit
summary: A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method enables accurate simulations of real quantum materials, bridging the gap between benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect in Hexagonal MnTe
summary: Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet isolates a single magnetic domain, revealing a sharp anomalous Hall effect and a sign reversal driven by modifications to the electronic Berry curvature.

title: Pseudogap, Fermi Liquid, Van Hove Singularity, and Maxima of the Compressibility and of the Knight Shift as a Function of Doping in the Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
summary: Analysis of Hubbard model simulations reveals that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.

title: Riemannian Geometric Classification and Emergent Phenomena of Magnetic Textures
summary: A classification framework based on differential geometry introduces geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron equations of motion in complex magnetic textures.

title: High-Dimensional Dynamics in Low-Dimensional Networks

title: Electric-Field Control of Interlayer Binding and Friction in $h$-BN Contacts

title: Lieb-Mattis States for Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
summary: A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.

title: Elastic and Structural Anisotropy in Silica Thin Films for Gravitational-Wave Detectors

title: Proof of the absence of local conserved quantities in general spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interaction

Thus, within this class, there is no intermediate possibility: a chain is either in a known integrable family, with infinitely many such charges, or has none.

title: Eightfold classification of superconducting orders
summary: Superconductivity begins when electrons bind into pairs. Because electrons are fermions, exchanging the two partners in a pair must flip the sign of its wavefunction — and that minus sign can be paid for in four different currencies: the pair’s spin, its spatial shape, its orbital character, and, less obviously, the relative time between the two electrons. Sharing one minus sign among four ± choices leaves exactly eight allowed kinds of Cooper pair. Balatsky and Banerjee show here that this eightfold rule is one face of a larger structure. A pair also has a center of mass — a place and a moment — and a superconductor can order in those as well. Taking internal shape (ρ), internal timing (τ), spatial modulation (R), and temporal modulation (T) as four independent axes builds the Berezinskii–Abrahams hypercube: a sixteen-corner map of superconducting order. BCS sits at the origin; each single axis recovers a familiar family — - and -wave gaps, odd-frequency pairing, FFLO and pair-density waves, driven superconductors. The corners in-between are hybrids. A few have been touched; most are empty, and the far corner, with all four switched-on at once, has never been visited. The hypercube is at once a classification and a search map.
